_comment: Atlas Growth :: UK home battery / backup-power installers from the MCS register (ICP-generators-uk.md option A, operator go 2026-09-30). Engine config for the google-maps-scrape BACK HALF only — there is no Maps scrape; pull-mcs.js writes mcs_leads.csv in the engine lead shape. Registry membership proves the trade (icp-source-planner R3), so the qualify stage is a NAME deny for national energy suppliers / social-housing arms plus a brand flag, and nothing else. No review floor (MCS rows carry no reviews). Domestic-vs-commercial is the site-text gate's call (STEP 5e), and no-website rows are FULLY USABLE here (the register supplies the email), so they are never a recovery track — they skip site text and go straight to Companies House + the MCS mailbox.

qualify_rules._r: 1. NAME deny — the national suppliers and social-housing / council arms the ICP doc says to drop (no homeowner-facing owner to sell a lead-gen retainer to; procurement, not a proprietor). Multi-word only, per the substring lesson: no bare 'sse' (Essex), no bare 'eon' (Aeon), no bare 'egg' (Gregg), no bare 'ovo' (Novo). 'social housing', 'housing association', 'council' catch the public-sector installers (British Gas Social Housing Ltd is on the register).
qualify_rules.label: national_supplier_or_public

brand_families._r: Roll-ups and national installers on the register — FLAG, never drop (operator standing directive). Substring test against name + root domain, so every term is distinctive. Add more at GATE 3 from collapse-domains.js location_count.

_r_site_l2_keywords: UK trade sites keep the mailbox on the contact page; battery/solar sites add survey/quote pages.

owner_query._r: UK bias terms; Companies House first (key on file), this is the residue pass.
